# Study 041: Mercurial Chemister, read against jaws-v1 (1-for-1, 10,000 paired games, Holm)
**Recommendation: NO CHANGE.** It is a five-drop that taps for two cards a turn from turn 6 at best. Every cut reads worse on draw, and on two of the three on damage too.
- for Brainstorm: damage @T10 212.1 -> 206.4 (-5.7 [-9.0, -2.4] Worse), killed by T6 -0.8 pts [-1.0, -0.5] Worse, extra cards by T8 -1.1 [-1.2, -1.0] Worse, hand can act by T3 -0.4 pts Worse. 1 better, 7 worse.
- for Willie Lumpkin: damage @T10 -7.4 [-10.4, -4.3] Worse, extra cards -0.9 [-1.1, -0.8] Worse, stall +0.8 pts Worse. 0 better, 8 worse: the cleanest "worse" of the nine screens.
- for Faerie Mastermind: damage @T10 -4.5 [-7.6, -1.3] no call, extra cards -0.8 [-0.9, -0.7] Worse, hoard @T10 +0.31 [+0.10, +0.51] Better, stall +0.7 pts Worse. 3 better, 7 worse.
- Why: it arrives on T5 and is summoning-sick, so it draws 2 on T6, then 2 a turn. By T8 that is 4-6 cards for 5 mana plus {U} a turn. The goldfish already counts that, and it still reads worse than a 1-mana Brainstorm, because the curve slot is the cost. The deck's 5-drop slot is Shabraz's turn.
- The goldfish is blind to the {R} discard-ping. It is repeatable creature removal (pings Krenko, Purphoros pingers, Tiny Bones' bodies), a real A-table job, and it pitches a wheel's dead hand. Unpriced, so this is a floor on that axis. It is still 5 mana and a tap the shark turn wants.
- Combos: I know of no two-card infinite with it. I did not run deck-combos on it.
- What would change the call: a table result where creature removal was the binding loss. The log's losses are 4 raced and 3 combo, so check whether a creature-answer was the missing card in those games.
- The ignored skeleton rows (S-bbe0cffb-07..13) are branch vs sleeved, not this card.
